description: Shorten the Muon momentum warmup from 300 steps to 100 steps.
Lower cautious Muon weight decay from 0.2 to 0.1.
Reduce TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**17 (a single 64x2048 micro-batch per step) to get many more optimizer steps in the 300 s budget.
Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.02 so the learning rate ramps up linearly over the first 2% of the time budget.
Lower EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.4 for the token embedding Adam optimizer.
Set WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.3 so the learning rate stays at its peak longer before decaying.
Add a learnable per-head scalar (init 1.2) multiplying q after QK RMS-norm, trained with AdamW without weight decay in its own scalar group (lr SCALAR_LR*0.01, as resid_lambdas).

description: Raise Muon MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.06 and cut Newton-Schulz iterations from 5 to 4, leaving Nesterov momentum on as the spec says to keep everything else unchanged.
Keep an fp32 EMA of all model parameters (decay min(0.999,(1+step)/(10+step)), updated each step with torch._foreach_lerp_) and copy it into the model just before the final evaluation.
Combine weight decay 0.1, total batch size 2**18 (2 micro-batches of 64x2048 per step), and a 2% LR warmup in one run.
Replace the linear LR warmdown with a cosine decay from 1 to FINAL_LR_FRAC over the warmdown period.
Set DEPTH=12 and ASPECT_RATIO=48 (model_dim rounds up to 640, 5 heads) and use DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 32 with 4-step gradient accumulation to stay safely within 40GB.
No change: train.py already sets TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**18 with DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64, which was the accepted slot 9 change.
Shrink the model to DEPTH=6 with ASPECT_RATIO=85 (model dim 512, 4 heads) so it gets more optimizer steps in the fixed 300 s.
No change: output projections are already zero-initialized and the lambdas already init at 1.0 and 0.1.

issues: The diff changes one hyperparameter: HEAD_DIM goes from 128 to 64. It does not touch the evaluation call, the data, the seed lines, the prepare.py import or the final summary printing. No integrity issue.
No bug that would make the result meaningless. model_dim = depth * 64, so it always divides evenly by HEAD_DIM 64. The only effect is twice as many heads, each half as wide.
The candidate scored 1.1041 against the incumbent's 1.0969, so it is 0.0072 worse. The negative z and the reject decision agree with that.

I can't recompute z exactly. Each side has only one run, so the noise estimate the harness used isn't in the numbers given. A z of -0.931 implies a noise scale of about 0.0077 (0.0072 / 0.931). That is plausible but I can't check it.

description: Set HEAD_DIM from 128 to 64 so the model has twice as many attention heads at the same width.
Halve SCALAR_LR from 0.5 to 0.25 for the per-layer scalar Adam parameters.
Lower cautious Muon WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.1 to 0.05, changing nothing else.
Set WARMDOWN_RATIO to 0.7 and FINAL_LR_FRAC to 0.05 so the LR decays linearly over the last 70% of training and ends at 5% of peak.
Clip the global gradient norm to 1.0 after the micro-batch backward passes and before optimizer.step(), leaving all learning rates unchanged.
Lower MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.03 for the Muon matrix parameters.
Set MATRIX_LR to 0.03 and UNEMBEDDING_LR to 0.008 together, changing nothing else.
